MC	<p>e7a8_381b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehn, +++, ehn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene X</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpx, +++, fpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5d73_d6e4</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene T</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, etx, +++, etx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ccc5_62cc</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fht, +++, fht"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>13f2_412f</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhp, +++, bhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>27f7_7986</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ace, +++, ace"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fnw, +++, fnw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ad23_d2b2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, amn, +++, amn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ef3f_b714</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfx, +++, cfx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>70a3_8bde</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, etx, +++, etx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>c4a9_6eca</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aef, +++, aef"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>119d_4aa8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene X</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, brx, +++, brx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a9c0_dbfa</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bek, +++, bek"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>510f_7e4d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bkr, +++, bkr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f400_c2ee</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene E</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ewx, +++, ewx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8c0f_525d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene H</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhk, +++, bhk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6c1c_f2ab</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene C</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cpy, +++, cpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>07e2_c840</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dpr, +++, dpr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2778_cb56</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #95336f;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #95336f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95336f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmw, +++, jmw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmy, +++, jmy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>5026_73ff</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdj, +++, bdj"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bd51_b717</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmr, +++, jmr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cbda_dbe2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdx, +++, cdx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6fad_3378</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene M</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene T</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene W</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mtw, +++, mtw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dpy, +++, dpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>07d6_c24b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene E</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, emy, +++, emy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>584c_ce09</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene A</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acf, +++, acf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d2c1_13d2</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpx, +++, fpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3a30_b5b5</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #95336f;">Gene M</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #95336f;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95336f;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfm, +++, bfm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cbf6_e443</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #95336f;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #95336f;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95336f;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfw, +++, cfw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #345f96;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fkm, +++, fkm"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2b11_4431</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #853994;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #853994;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #853994;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acf, +++, acf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>49ed_9b83</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhr, +++, bhr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bhp, +++, bhp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2355_d75a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene F</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fnp, +++, fnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8eb6_6fe0</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehp, +++, ehp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>87c3_7853</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene D</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdk, +++, bdk"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>89c8_8af1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #973f25;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #973f25;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #973f25;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #874d18;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #874d18;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #874d18;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1c702a;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1c702a;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #00668d;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #00668d;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cex, +++, cex"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9e3b_bd3d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene M</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene R</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mnr, +++, mnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>cae0_b38a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006f52;">Gene P</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006f52;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006f52;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, mpx, +++, mpx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene W</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene X</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, rwx, +++, rwx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>60b1_eb4a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #95336f;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #95336f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype.
