The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene A</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene R</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene T</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, art, +++, art"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #95336f;">Gene Y</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #95336f;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #95336f;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kry, +++, kry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene D</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #9e3146;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #9e3146;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene N</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6b5f00;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6b5f00;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #345f96;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #345f96;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #795716;">Gene C</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #795716;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #795716;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #046c68;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #046c68;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #046c68;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #404dc8;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #404dc8;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjt, +++, cjt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>a87d_b712</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #53671a;">Gene B</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #53671a;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #53671a;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #096979;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #096979;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #096979;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6b43ae;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6b43ae;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype.
